name: Artiguism
summary: Artiguism is the programme of José Gervasio Artigas and the Oriental Revolution in the River Plate: independence from Spain and Portugal, a republic of separated powers, and a confederation of sovereign provinces opposed to Buenos Aires centralism. It combined civil and religious liberty, free trade among provinces and through free ports, armed provincial militias, and a 1815 land reform favouring the poor, free Black people, Indigenous people and landless Creoles.
scope: The political and social programme of Artigas c. 1811-1820, based on the Instructions of the Year XIII, the 1815 Reglamento de Tierras and the League of Free Peoples. It is a historical, regional federalist-republican doctrine; modern statements outside that period are inferred and mostly low confidence. It excludes later uses of Artigas's name by Uruguayan parties.

sources.title: Las verdaderas raíces del proyecto Artigas (on the 1815 Reglamento, citing historian José Rilla)
sources.author: La Nación
sources.usedFor: The 1815 Reglamento de Tierras: conditional land grants to free Black people, zambos, Indigenous people and poor Creoles; vagrancy and worker-paper rules; historians' interpretation.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a 1810s concern; the program's priority for the poorest suggests sympathy for state provision, but this is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage policy was not addressed; the Reglamento instead gave land and required employers to register workers, so there is no basis to lean either way.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Reglamento had the provincial authority allot land and control rural labour, which cuts against trusting markets alone, though free inter-provincial trade was welcomed.

public-ownership.rationale: Public land and treasury estates were redistributed, but industry and utilities did not exist in the program; adherents would not obviously take a side.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Confiscating emigrant and royalist estates was punitive, not an income tax program; no stated view on wealth taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Labour unions did not exist in the Río de la Plata of 1815; nothing can be inferred beyond sympathy for rural workers.

property-fundamental.rationale: Estates of emigrants and royalists were expropriated and land grants could not be sold, so property was subordinate to the province's needs.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations in the modern sense were absent; no basis for a position.

cut-welfare.rationale: Making the most unfortunate the most privileged in land grants runs against cutting aid to the poor, though the grants demanded work.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; the Reglamento required worker papers and vagrant banishment but that is rural order, not anti-terror surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not a question of the period and the program is silent.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Instruction 3 asked for civil liberty to the fullest imaginable extent, which a modern adherent would likely read as hostile to speech restrictions.

strong-leader.rationale: The Instructions demand separated, mutually independent powers and warn against military despotism, though Artigas himself ruled as Protector.

state-harmful.rationale: The Instructions set up a state of provincial governments plus a Supreme Government with separated powers; abolishing the state is contrary to its design.

limit-guns.rationale: Instruction 17 says the right of the peoples to keep arms must not be violated and calls for provincial militias.

empower-police-military.rationale: Instruction 18 seeks constitutional limits against abusive military power, favouring militias over a strong standing force.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed by the sources, and the Reglamento's vagrancy rules point to no clear view.

decide-locally.rationale: Instructions 4, 7 and 11 reserve all but general affairs to each province, which keeps sovereignty; federalism is the core of the doctrine.

rehabilitation.rationale: The Reglamento punished vagrancy with banishment but also offered land for productive reintegration; no penal doctrine is documented.

traditional-family.rationale: Artigas operated within a Catholic rural society and the ideology has no recorded challenge to traditional family norms.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; a committed adherent of the 1810s Catholic setting would be unlikely to endorse it, though modern Uruguayan Artiguists may.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Catholic context of the period, with no documented position.

more-religion-public.rationale: Instruction 3 promotes religious liberty to the greatest degree, which suggests no established dominance of religion in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The Reglamento granted land to free Black people, zambos, Indigenous people and poor Creoles ahead of others. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; no inference possible from the program.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The movement stressed the autonomy of the peoples and provinces more than a cultural tradition, and does not address this directly.

gradual-change.rationale: Artiguism was a revolutionary movement breaking from Spain and Buenos Aires centralism, so respect for established institutions was not its approach.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration policy was not an issue of the program.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: International organisations did not exist; the confederation principle is about provinces, not global bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Instructions 12 to 14 declared Maldonado and Colonia free ports and removed duties between provinces, and Artiguism pursued a free-trade treaty with Britain.

nation-first.rationale: The question of global cooperation did not arise; the movement was committed to regional independence and alliance among provinces.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; Instruction 10 provides for mutual defence among provinces only.

open-borders.rationale: Instruction 9 insists on reclaiming Misiones and border towns held by Portugal, showing concern for territorial integrity.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental limits were not a concern of the period.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate change was unknown in the 1810s and Artiguist texts say nothing on environmental policy, so no stance can be inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The programme says nothing about technology's promise; its remedies were institutional and agrarian, so adherents would not clearly agree.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power postdates the movement by over a century and no principle of the programme bears on it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Artiguism is the programme of the Oriental Revolution against Spain, Portugal and Buenos Aires centralism, with independence as its first demand.

experts-over-public.rationale: The Instructions rest sovereignty on the peoples and their provincial governments rather than on a learned elite.

central-planning.rationale: Instruction 7 limits the Supreme Government to general affairs, so a centrally planned economy runs against the federal design.

socialized-markets.rationale: The Reglamento granted land to small producers, but no stance on worker or public ownership of firms is documented.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land was distributed rather than taxed; no tax doctrine is recorded.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Instruction 15 deals with the province's claim to unclaimed foreign estates, but not with taxing large inheritances.

basic-income.rationale: Cash transfers were unknown; the Reglamento gave land conditional on work, which points away from unconditional payment but not decisively.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Instruction 14 bars duties between provinces and the free ports invite foreign ships, though livestock exports to Brazil were banned.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The provincial authority steered land use and ranching, but industrial investment is not documented.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The 1815 Reglamento assigned estancia plots to free Black people, Indigenous people and poor Creoles, spreading holdings among small owners, though Rilla reads it chiefly as a measure for order and production.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Reglamento regulated wage labour by requiring employers to register workers, treating it as a normal institution.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Central banking did not exist in the Banda Oriental of 1815 and the sources discuss customs revenue, not money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The political order was territorial federalism with elected governments, not state-recognised class bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Instructions 5, 6 and 20 prescribe separated powers and a republican form, incompatible with a single ruling party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Artigas is described as opposed to monarchism, and Instruction 20 guarantees a republican form of government.

democracy-best.rationale: Artigas is described as a staunch democrat, though the sources do not discuss voters choosing badly.

direct-votes.rationale: The Congress of Oriente and cabildos were assemblies, but referendums on laws are not documented.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power in the Instructions rests with provincial governments and a Congress, not councils of workers.

right-to-secede.rationale: Instruction 11 retains provincial sovereignty and independence beyond delegated powers, but the programme sought a confederation rather than secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: His egalitarian land grants and republicanism are at odds with a belief in naturally superior rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Artiguists took up arms in a revolutionary war, so pacifism is excluded.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed as a doctrine; war was a necessity of independence.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Instructions promote religious liberty but do not call for strict separation, and the society was Catholic.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Instructions ground authority in provincial constitutions and republican government, not scripture, and endorse religious liberty.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Instructions require three public powers, including a judicial one, and provincial militias under public command.

military-superiority.rationale: Instruction 10 sets up mutual defence among provinces; the sources do not describe any aim of superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Reglamento welcomed Indigenous, Black, mixed-race and Creole settlers on equal terms, so a single-ethnicity nation was not the aim.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Reglamento sought order and productive use of land rather than class conflict, and La Nacion notes historians dispute a social-revolution reading.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Priority for the poor was real, but equality of outcomes is not a stated aim.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous people received individual land grants, not collective authority; no stated view on traditional lands.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The programme sought freedom from Spanish rule and Portuguese occupation but never demanded compensation from them.

civilizational-union.rationale: The union sought was among the provinces of the River Plate, not across civilisations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Artigas refused bribes and spoke of serving the nation rather than his own reward, suggesting a civic ethic.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Instructions foreground liberty and equality of citizens and peoples, with civil liberty to the greatest imaginable degree.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources treat land as a productive resource for settlers and give no view on nature's value apart from use.

limit-population.rationale: The territory was sparsely populated and settlement was welcomed; an inference only.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Industry was absent from the pastoral River Plate economy of the time, and the programme neither praised nor condemned it.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technological disruption was not a theme; the movement focused on land, trade and constitutional form.

human-enhancement.rationale: Body and mind enhancement is outside anything the 1810s programme could have addressed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: AI government is wholly anachronistic, and the Instructions' emphasis on elected provincial governments gives no lead.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption is anachronistic and no Artiguist text bears on private communication.

restore-past-order.rationale: The programme was a break with colonial and centralist order toward federal republic.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Artigas's documents are principled (confederation, liberty), but the sources do not say whether adherents judged policy by results.

direct-action.rationale: Artiguists used both congresses and armed action, so adherents would not simply favour direct action over assemblies.

means-match-ends.rationale: Neither the Instructions nor the Reglamento discuss whether methods should mirror the society sought.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Settled agriculture and ranching were the basis of the programme, making it the opposite of foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The Reglamento organised ranching, estates and wage workers, treating labour division as normal.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Priority to the unfortunate was real, but the programme tied grants to work and conduct, not to need alone.

production-for-use.rationale: The Reglamento stressed productive use of land and its economic aims, with no stance on profit versus use.

profit-exploitation.rationale: No Marxist theory; the Reglamento took wage labour as normal and sought productive ranching.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Instructions prescribe separated powers and republican government, excluding any class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Land was assigned to individual families who had to build a dwelling and corrals, so collective farming was not the model.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Capitalism and imperialism as a theory belong to later Marxism, and the programme invites free trade rather than denounces it.

taxation-theft.rationale: Instruction 12 creates a customs house at Maldonado and the province raises its own revenue, so taxation is accepted.

harm-principle.rationale: Civil liberty was to be promoted widely, but the Reglamento also punished vagrancy, so a pure harm principle is not stated.

conscription.rationale: Provincial militias were authorised, but compulsory service is not discussed in the sources read.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Instructions speak of the liberties of both citizens and peoples, so rights are not purely individual.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The programme relied on voice through provincial government and congresses, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The state in the Instructions is a federal republic serving liberty and equality, not a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Reglamento gave land so that the poor could support themselves, an early material-means conception of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Universities and mass media in the modern sense did not exist, so the claim has no counterpart in the programme.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The program extended land to Black, Indigenous and mixed people, treating them as capable settlers. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation was through provincial governments and the congress; the cabildos are mentioned but corporate bodies are not.

total-state.rationale: Instruction 7 limits the Supreme Government to general matters and Instruction 3 defends civil liberty; total state control is excluded.

national-rebirth.rationale: The programme looked to constitutional and federal reorganisation rather than rebirth after decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Instruction 9 claims Misiones for the Oriental Province, but that is recovery, not expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Instructions require republican, constitutional government with separate powers, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: The Reglamento granted land freely to the landless and regulated employers; binding farmers to a lord contradicts it.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology of this kind is absent from the sources, and Enlightenment influences point if anything the other way.

universal-morality.rationale: Artigas drew on Enlightenment authors, who held reason-based universal rights, so a modest lean to agree is inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Federalism accepts competing provincial interests, but the programme also states general interests of the state.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism has no connection with the River Plate programme, which never addressed it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return was not an issue; the nearest topic is the Reglamento's treatment of emigrants' estates, which were confiscated rather than protected.

revive-national-language.rationale: Spanish was the shared language and the sources report no language-revival aim.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Large companies were absent, and the sources give no stance on workers voting in firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Public schooling policy is not documented in the sources read, and vouchers were not a contemporary idea.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Keynesian stimulus is a modern debate; the sources say only that the province would raise its own customs revenue.

economic-freedom.rationale: Free ports and free internal trade show a commitment to economic liberty alongside political liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Instructions rely on constitutions and separated powers rather than rulers' example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Instruction 1 demands absolute independence and Instruction 11 preserves the sovereignty of each people.

force-without-un.rationale: The UN is a twentieth-century body; the programme speaks only of mutual defence among provinces.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Land grants went to free people of all backgrounds in the province, but welfare for immigrants is not discussed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Land grants were conditional on work, building a rancho and corrals, and employers had to register workers.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Reglamento sought order and productive ranching, with employers and workers under shared provincial rules rather than class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; no sign of hostility to inherited institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: The programme's regional alliance was among the River Plate provinces, not a bloc of states dominated by Western powers.

workers-nation.rationale: National versus international working-class organisation is a later Marxist debate that the sources do not touch.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: No documented position on law and gender roles.

ban-interest.rationale: The sources report no objection to lending at interest, and free ports and trade imply ordinary commercial credit.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Land was granted to Black, Indigenous, zambo and Creole settlers alike, which excludes segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Instructions treat the state as a republic serving liberty and equality, not as a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Fossil fuel production was not part of the economy or the programme; no inference is possible.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration and assimilation are not discussed, though the Reglamento welcomed varied poor settlers as they were.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in the programme.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not specified in the Instructions beyond provincial and national legislative powers.

national-mission.rationale: Instructions stress each province's sovereignty and independence, not a mission to spread a system elsewhere.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The sources never discuss the position of women in these terms, apart from naming needy widows among land recipients.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Artigas channelled rural discontent against colonial authorities and Buenos Aires centralists, though the sources do not state this in general terms.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is alien to a programme that welcomed all poor settlers.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Instruction 18 limits military power constitutionally, but accountability for past abuses is not discussed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The provincial government allotted land and regulated labour, so its role was wider than defence and justice.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mixed-race people, zambos and Black people were named beneficiaries of land grants.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Instruction 4 aims at the equality, liberty and security of citizens and peoples.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialist theory is outside the programme, so the question has no counterpart.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The question about settler states is modern; the sources only note land grants to Indigenous people and others in the province.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Instruction 3 gives religious liberty but the sources do not say whether civil law was to be uniform across religions.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Instruction 3 promotes religious liberty to the fullest extent imaginable.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: The Reglamento was about expanding cattle ranching, so banning slaughter contradicts the economy it promoted.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religious liberty was favoured, but education is not documented.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist state under capitalist encirclement is a Soviet-era question with no counterpart in the sources.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Instructions rest sovereignty on the peoples and provincial constitutions; Artigas is called a democrat and republican.

trade-surplus.rationale: Free ports and open trade suggest no mercantilist target, but nothing is stated.

population-transfer.rationale: The Reglamento aimed to settle and include Indigenous, Black and poor residents, not expel them.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The movement fought wars, but the sources do not present any doctrine on initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist ideas are absent from the sources; the programme speaks of liberty, equality and security.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Parties in the modern sense were not yet formed and the programme says nothing on outlawing them.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican Instructions guard provinces against usurpation and military despotism, close to a non-domination idea.

separated-powers.rationale: Instructions 5 and 6 divide government into legislative, executive and judicial powers that may not be united.

vanguard-party.rationale: Federal republican institutions are incompatible with a disciplined revolutionary vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Reglamento's article 6 says the most unfortunate will be the most privileged in land grants.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is a modern British issue with no connection to the sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes and picketing were not features of the rural River Plate economy of the time.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The programme treated poverty as a matter of land access, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Policies included Black, Indigenous, mixed and Creole people on shared terms.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not mentioned; the Instructions assume elected governments and a republican constitution.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Instructions stress constitutional limits and civil liberty, though wartime leadership acted firmly.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The sources mention no price fixing, though the Reglamento did regulate rural labour and land.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Instructions promote civil liberty and separation of powers, which a state-controlled press contradicts.

party-commands-army.rationale: Instruction 18 limits military power by constitutional rules and Instruction 17 relies on provincial militias.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not covered by the Instructions or the Reglamento.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The sources do not discuss pay of officials.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Modern political parties are absent; delegates carried instructions from their provinces, but party discipline is not discussed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Instruction 11 has provinces delegate expressly some powers to the Congress of the United Provinces within a confederation. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Instruction 18 limits military power but does not say who commands.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the Instructions, which address only religious liberty in general terms.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Instructions set out republican separated powers and religious liberty, with no clerical authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The movement was itself a government at war, so working-class defeatism was not its approach.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Instruction 3 on civil liberty to the fullest imaginable extent runs against censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not mentioned in the sources, though Artigas was elected Protector by congress.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is not mentioned, though Artigas's republicanism may allow it; no source states a position.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Instruction 10 entails alliance among provinces, and the programme cultivated a British treaty, so neither end nor keep is clear.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Land was granted for individual rancho building, but abolishing rentals is not part of the programme.

people-in-arms.rationale: Instruction 17 gives provinces the right to raise militias and says the peoples' right to keep arms may not be violated.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Artigas drew his support from gauchos and rural people and promoted rural settlement.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Instruction 9 demands that Misiones and border towns held by Portugal return to the Oriental Province.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectual populism is not part of the documented programme, whose Instructions drew on Paine and Rousseau.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The sources show no doctrine on cultural hierarchy, though the Reglamento treated all groups as eligible settlers.

death-penalty.rationale: The sources read do not mention capital punishment, and no inference to adherents' view is possible.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School curricula on sex education are absent from the period; no inference possible.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Evolution was not yet a debate in the 1810s; the programme is silent on school curricula.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pornography regulation is not discussed in the sources.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules by descent versus birth are not stated; the Instructions speak of citizens and peoples without defining them.

minority-language-support.rationale: Languages other than Spanish, such as Guarani among Indigenous people, are not mentioned in the programme.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious liberty was a principle, but exemptions from general law are not discussed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's argument about custom is not part of the sources; Instruction 3's liberty is political and religious.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt was not at issue, and the sources do not mention loans.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Reglamento linked independence to land reform and protecting the rural poor, though it is not framed in these terms.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Instruction 16 gives the province its own constitution and a part in making the general constitution, and the Congress of Oriente was an elected assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Reglamento aimed to promote production and order but no statement on trading freedoms for growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid is a modern idea with no counterpart in the sources.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement by well over a century.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Instructions do not say how the executive is chosen, only that powers are separate and the form republican.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banks did not exist, so the programme has no position.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Instruction 9 insists on reclaiming territory held by Portugal; inferred for peace deals.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Estates of emigrants were reassigned and grants were conditional on use, showing property serving the province's good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet debate is unrelated to Artiguism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is not part of the programme.

collective-defense.rationale: Instruction 10 commits each province to assist any other attacked, for any reason, in a defensive league.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Instruction 9 treats Portuguese-held towns as lawfully belonging to the province; inferred to annexations generally.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Instructions promote religious liberty, not curbs on church property or power.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not discuss a ceremonial head of state; Artigas was himself an executive leader.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Provincial sovereignty and voluntary confederation point against coercion, though Artigas fought centralists.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Instructions 11, 15 and 16 let a province keep its own constitution and rules while joining the confederation.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Artigas was a republican who opposed monarchy, and the Instructions require a republican form of government.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income tax did not exist; the sources mention customs duties only.

character-from-environment.rationale: Enlightenment influences and land grants to improve conditions suggest this leaning, inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Instruction 20 and Instructions 5 and 6 bind every power to a republican constitution.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is a modern idea; nothing in the sources bears on it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The republican frame with separated powers draws on popular sovereignty, not rule by a few.

leader-cult.rationale: Artigas refused rewards and spoke of serving the nation, and the programme is republican.

equal-parenting.rationale: Child custody law is not discussed in the sources.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Socialism under party leadership is a Marxist-Leninist debate outside the sources.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Reglamento assigned estates to the landless, including confiscated lands of emigrants, though La Nacion notes it did not seize all large estates.

refugee-return.rationale: Return of refugees is not documented, though the Reglamento dealt with the estates of those who emigrated.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Instruction 9 bases the claim on provincial territory, not on the nationality of its inhabitants.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religious liberty was a founding demand in Instruction 3.

women-must-cover.rationale: Civil and religious liberty point against such compulsion; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not mentioned in the Instructions' provisions on trade among provinces.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The union sought was among provinces of the River Plate, not among peoples of a language family.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Cultural autonomy of national minorities is not in the sources; provincial autonomy is.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The question concerns a diaspora minority and has no counterpart in the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism is not part of Artiguist thought, whose influences were Enlightenment and US federalist writers.

ban-cartels.rationale: Cartels and economic concentration in the modern sense are absent from the sources.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm bailouts are modern and not discussed.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Instructions create an independent judiciary and constitutional limits on power.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for women in public bodies are unconnected to the period; women's political role is not documented.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Free ports and free trade among provinces point away from a closed bloc, though livestock export to Brazil was banned.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Labour and environmental clauses in trade agreements are modern; Instruction 14 simply wants unburdened trade among provinces.

moral-incentives.rationale: Guevarist moral incentives are not part of the programme, which tied land to conditions of work and conduct.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The revolution was a mass rural uprising, not a foco, and it is unclear which analogy adherents would pick.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Artigas was an anti-monarchist republican and the Reglamento gave privilege to the unfortunate, so hereditary titles are opposed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: School curricula are not addressed in the sources read.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Instruction 1 demands absolute independence from Spain and rejects rule by another power.

patriotic-education.rationale: Education policy is not documented in the sources read, so no position is stated.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The Reglamento gave land to Black, Indigenous and zambo settlers first, a preference for disadvantaged groups.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation by banks or states is not a topic in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalist crises and collapse are not a concern of the programme.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The programme sought independence from Spain, not influence over former dominions.

delink-world-market.rationale: Instructions 12 and 13 open free ports to foreign shipping, so cutting ties is opposed.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The thesis about rich-country workers is a Leninist concept with no counterpart here.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Reglamento granted land across racial lines, and civil liberty is in the Instructions, but private discrimination is not discussed.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Instruction 16 calls for a written constitution and Instruction 3 for civil liberty; a firm bill of rights is inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The sources do not discuss annulling colonial treaties, though Instruction 1 dissolves ties with the Spanish Crown.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Instructions create a republic with elected provincial and national governments, and Artigas opposed monarchism.

minority-veto.rationale: The Instructions provide majority rule within constituted powers and a confederation pact among provinces, not individual vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Instruction 20 protects provinces against usurpation of rights, and Artigas rebelled against Buenos Aires despotism.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Instructions give a legislature but also balanced powers, so legislative supremacy is not stated.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not discussed, and the economy was cattle ranching, so no stance can be inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The Reglamento promotes ranching and the economy depended on livestock, but the sources do not discuss humane standards.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The Reglamento did not rest on charity from privileged people, and no duty is stated.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Artigas was a political and military leader, committed to public action.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt School theory is absent from the sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not part of the programme.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is anachronistic and the programme invites foreign trade through free ports.

native-born-offices.rationale: Offices for native-born citizens only are not mentioned in the sources.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist parties choosing their own road is unrelated to the River Plate programme.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Foreign aid did not exist; the programme sought free trade, not autarky or aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Instruction 9 demands the return of Misiones and border towns occupied by the Portuguese.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous people were beneficiaries of land, but political leadership is not discussed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fascism postdates Artigas by a century; no inference is available.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The equivalence debate about fascism and communism is outside the sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The American Civil War is unrelated to the programme.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument disputes are not part of the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's issues are not addressed; the sources on gender mention only widows as land recipients.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not documented in the programme.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Artiguism borrowed US and French institutions explicitly, but the sources say nothing on whether civilizations need distinct ones.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Instruction 18 aims to prevent military despotism through constitutional limits.

paid-care-work.rationale: Domestic labour as paid work is a modern feminist idea absent from the sources.

filial-duty.rationale: The sources do not describe family duties between generations.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service examinations are not mentioned; the sources assume elected officials.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign firms buying strategic industries has no counterpart in the 1810s economy.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not documented; the setting was Catholic, but adherents' position is unknown.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Representatives came with mandates (the Instructions themselves were a mandate to the 1813 Assembly), implying delegates bound to those who chose them.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pensions were not part of the programme.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land was assigned conditionally and not saleable, but grantees held it for use; full community ownership is not stated.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Instruction 12 creates customs revenue for the province but the sources do not give budget procedures.

single-official-language.rationale: Official language policy is not mentioned.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The Reglamento aimed land at local settlers, but foreign owners are not discussed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine is a modern legal concept the programme does not address.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumer culture is not discussed; free ports sought imports of goods, with no moral criticism recorded.

corporate-influence.rationale: Corporate lobbying did not exist, and the programme is silent on firm influence.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Artiguism received foreign contacts but the sources describe no policy of arming insurgents elsewhere.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Instruction 11 stresses provincial sovereignty; troops entering without consent would violate it.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding of NGOs and media has no counterpart in the sources.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy is not discussed, though the Reglamento encouraged settlement of the land.

residents-only-property.rationale: Estates of emigrants were redistributed to locals, in line with local priority for land.

job-guarantee.rationale: State employer-of-last-resort policy is absent; the Reglamento gave land to those willing to work it.

democratic-peace.rationale: The sources do not discuss democracies and war; the Instructions provide only for provincial mutual defence.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Philosophical anarchism on obedience is not part of the programme, which sought lawful republican government.

non-intervention.rationale: Provincial sovereignty and independence in Instruction 11 and independence from Spain imply non-intervention, though Artiguists did seek allies.

industrial-unions.rationale: Unions of any kind were not present in the setting.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy ideas have no place in the documented programme.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Catholic setting.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information laws are not in the sources.

local-production.rationale: Free trade measures point the other way, so no clear position.

informal-organisation.rationale: The programme was institutional with congresses, provincial governments and militias.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The sources do not discuss international law; they assert provincial sovereignty and independence.

religious-nation.rationale: Instruction 3's religious liberty excludes defining the community by shared religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Instruction 1 demands absolute independence and equality among provinces.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Instruction 15 and the provincial sovereignty principle keep provincial revenues under provincial control.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Land grants were to individuals with their own rancho and corrals.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communism did not exist as a political force in the period.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery models are not discussed.

religion-illusion.rationale: Artigas lived within a Catholic order and defended religious liberty rather than rejecting religion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Marxist assessment of capitalism is not part of the sources.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Women's equality as a goal is not discussed in the sources.

socialized-care.rationale: Public childcare and housework are absent from the programme.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not documented in the sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, beyond the treaty-based confederation pact.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Settlers were individual families, not cooperatives, but small communities of settlers have some resemblance.

majority-settlement.rationale: The Reglamento invited many groups to settle, not majority colonisation of minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third positions between capitalism and communism are later concepts; the sources do not speak to it.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Instruction 9 bases claims to Misiones and border towns on belonging to the province.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the programme; inferred as rejection.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The sources are silent on sexual conduct and its legal treatment.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Instructions favour civil liberty and separation of powers, though vagrants were banished.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Instruction 3 on religious liberty weighs against punishing practice of other religions.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Instruction 1 demands independence from Spain and freedom from obligations to the Crown.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Islamic doctrine is unconnected to the River Plate programme.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The Instructions ground rule in republican constitutions, not religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Popular assemblies such as the Congress of Oriente and cabildos suggest sympathy, though no doctrine is stated.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality is a modern theory absent from the sources, though the Reglamento did name several disadvantaged groups together.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Gender identity law is anachronistic, with nothing in the sources to infer from.

assisted-dying.rationale: Medical assistance in dying is not discussed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The left-right spectrum emerged in France and is not discussed in the sources.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's concept of alienation is absent from the sources.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Religious liberty and absence of cultural-essentialist claims point to rejection, inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Instructions ground sovereignty in the provinces and peoples, with Rousseau and Paine as influences.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Dress codes in state institutions are not discussed, though Instruction 3 stresses religious liberty.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Nondisclosure agreements and arbitration are modern employment law outside the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Ordoliberal social markets are twentieth-century concepts not in the sources.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Instruction 17 explicitly provides for provincial regiments and militias.

rich-first.rationale: The Reglamento favoured the poor first, the reverse of this priority.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Rival military blocs did not exist; the sources offer only provincial mutual defence.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Instruction 20 requires a republican government, and Artigas opposed monarchy; hereditary office has no place.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist credit is not discussed in the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: International lender conditionality is modern and absent from the sources.

property-franchise.rationale: Voting qualifications are not defined in the Instructions, so the position is not documented.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist claims are outside the sources.

reification.rationale: Lukacs's concept is a modern Marxist idea outside the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The sources discuss civil liberty broadly but not press ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Instructions 5, 6 and 16 establish a constitution, separated powers and an independent judiciary.

racial-franchise.rationale: Policies extended standing to Black, Indigenous and mixed people.

online-participation.rationale: Online deliberation is anachronistic, with nothing in the sources to infer from.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data records are modern and not discussed.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religious liberty in Instruction 3 weighs against such restrictions.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Religious liberty and equality make a boycott on communal lines inconsistent.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition assemblies are not mentioned; the elected Congress of Oriente is the documented model.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Doctrinal reform is not discussed, though Instruction 3 guarantees religious liberty.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Reglamento redistributed large holdings of emigrants and royalists to the poor, implying concern about concentrated holdings.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The sources are silent on sexual orientation and the military.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Instruction 3 promotes religious liberty, and a state atheism is the opposite.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Reglamento enforced order with banishment and worker papers, taking public order for granted.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational arrangements are modern; the programme's equivalent is provincial equality in a confederation.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The provincial authority itself assigned land to the poor.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits for politicians are not discussed in the sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is anachronistic and not in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is a modern concern outside the programme.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Church office and gender are not discussed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Marital authority law is not documented in the sources.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The sources do not discuss voting by foreign residents.

rent-control.rationale: Rent regulation is not in the sources; the Reglamento addressed rural land grants.

abolish-ip.rationale: Patents and copyrights were not part of the setting or the programme.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inconsistent with civil liberty and republican principles; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear weapons are far outside the period.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed beyond independence; no foreign basing existed.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Formal genocide recognition is a modern practice; the sources do not discuss it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Reglamento tied land grants to work and conduct, and gave them to those who would farm it themselves.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Armed defence of the province was central, so pacifism is excluded.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Artigas's programme drew on Enlightenment ideas rather than claims of ancient national origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The sociology of sex is a modern topic absent from the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory debates are outside the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The sources record no cult of martyrs; Artigas is cited as refusing personal reward.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The programme is constitutional and secular in design.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The programme does not discuss diasporas or cultural centres.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Instructions put political independence and constitution-making first.

god-not-male.rationale: Theological language is not discussed in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist scriptural criticism is outside the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Land went to settlers of all backgrounds; no ethnic economic claim is stated.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Instruction 8 unifies the territory as one Oriental Province, but this is not a general principle.

independent-unions.rationale: Trade unions were not present in the setting.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Socialist definitions are not part of Artiguist thought.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Water and hospital provision are not documented in the programme.

second-chamber.rationale: The Instructions give a legislative power in both national and provincial government but do not describe a second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Land went to families, not municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Instructions 2, 10 and 11 require a confederation of provinces with delegated powers to a Congress.

family-wage.rationale: Family wage policy is not discussed, though the Reglamento regulated employers' duties toward workers.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is anachronistic with no counterpart in the sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Life-extension research is outside the period and programme.

person-over-state.rationale: Instruction 4 says governments exist to conserve the equality, liberty and security of citizens.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The sources do not state a theory of human spiritual nature, though society was Catholic.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Instruction 11 says provinces retain sovereignty except for powers they delegate; the centre cannot revoke them.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning questions are absent from the sources, which are about rural settlement.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Reglamento treated people of all races as co-beneficiaries.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in ancestry is not addressed, and the Reglamento stressed inclusion of different groups instead.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Instruction 10 is a defensive alliance, and Artiguists fought to defend the province.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Instructions define the polity by provinces and peoples, not language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Provincial and national governments were territorial, not communal.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Instructions fear Portuguese and Spanish occupation and Buenos Aires centralism, but state no general plot of partition.

free-public-college.rationale: University education is not discussed in the sources.

future-generations.rationale: Intergenerational environmental duty is not discussed in the sources.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Gendered political values are not discussed in the sources.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Instructions authorise militias and arms, with no talk of arms reduction.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Republican, popular sovereignty would favour public treaties; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital movement controls are anachronistic; the sources cover goods trade through free ports.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Instruction 17 protects the peoples' right to keep arms and provincial militias.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The movement depended on soldiers fighting in defence of the province.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Collective bargaining requires unions and industrial employers who did not exist in the setting.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Income tax credits are modern and unrelated to the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal rules are modern and not in the sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: A new international economic order is a twentieth-century demand absent from the sources.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Artiguism founded its own provincial governments and federal institutions rather than speaking of smashing the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Provincial sovereignty and the right to a separate constitution allow each province its own regime.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Instructions are a secular constitutional programme.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student loans do not feature in the period.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Artiguism arose in opposition to Buenos Aires centralism, which it saw as dominating the provinces.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Enlightenment influences imply shared rights, inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Public broadcasters are modern and absent from the sources.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Perennialism is not discussed, though Instruction 3's liberty applies to all religions.

farm-price-support.rationale: Rural production was central, but price support is not documented.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear arms are far outside the period.

workers-own-party.rationale: Working-class parties did not exist in the setting.

ban-fgm.rationale: The sources do not mention FGM, a practice that did not feature in the region.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Reglamento mentions needy widows among those receiving grants, but equal inheritance is not addressed.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Linguistic naming disputes are not in the sources.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Environmental tort law is modern and not in the sources.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Indigenous chiefs are not given any role in the Instructions or the Reglamento, so no stance is documented.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmental trade-offs with liberty are not in the sources.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Sentencing policy is not documented in the sources.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language requirements for immigrants are not discussed.

voter-id.rationale: Voter identification is modern and not in the sources.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Instruction 3 promotes religious liberty, implying no single interpretation holds legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The sources do not define democracy, though they call for elected republican institutions.

premarital-sex.rationale: Sexual morality is not documented in the programme.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Negative income tax is a twentieth-century proposal outside the sources.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not addressed; women's suffrage did not exist in the period, so any answer is inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from respect for religion.

race-social-construct.rationale: Racial concepts in this sense are modern, though the Reglamento treated Black, zambo, Indigenous and Creole settlers alike.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Gender ministries are modern and not documented in the sources.

worker-ownership.rationale: The Reglamento assigned land to individual families and required employers to register workers, so wage employment under owners was assumed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Artigas read Paine and Rousseau but acted within a Catholic society and defended religious liberty rather than reason alone as the sole guide.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The 1815 Reglamento granted land through the authorities, conditional on settling and working it, rather than making the first claimant its owner.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the programme's republican rule of law and separated powers.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the Instructions' civil and religious liberty, which does not make one literal reading of scripture binding on all.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Women's participation was not addressed in the 1810s programme; no answer can be inferred either way.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the programme's rejection of centralised rule and its private smallholder land reform.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from the confederation's congresses of delegates sent by provinces and towns, though the sources do not describe the voting method.

national-church-status.rationale: The Instructions promote civil and religious liberty, which points to equal standing for religious bodies.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the confederal principle of sovereign provinces running their own affairs; ethnic minorities as such were not the frame.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of popular and provincial sovereignty, under which peoples choose their own association.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: the League of Free Peoples was built from the colonial provinces as they stood, within a confederation.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the Reglamento's aim of settling the poor on working smallholdings, and Artigas's own austere frontier life.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The Reglamento favoured Indigenous people in land grants but did not restrict outside settlement; the sources give no clear position.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: the programme's armed provincial militias were of male citizens, and equal drafting of women was not conceived.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Artigas's programme defended the 'patria' of the Orientales and its land, but no text frames a spiritual bond; inferred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The Instructions of the Year XIII require a republic of separated powers and civil liberty, which rules out killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic: the programme had no China policy, only opposition to Spanish and Portuguese rule and Buenos Aires centralism.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Not an Artiguist theme; the programme concerned provincial confederation, not co-nationals under other states.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The 1815 land reform gave land to the poor under a rule that the most unfortunate be the most privileged; a sympathy for shared land access is inferred.

self-ownership.rationale: Civil liberty was a core aim and Artigas freed and enlisted slaves, so personal freedom is favoured; no text states a self-ownership doctrine.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Artiguism opposed internal duties but did not address consumption taxes on goods; no clear answer.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The Reglamento privileged the poorest, such as free Black people, Indigenous people and landless Creoles, which suggests targeting; inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Artigas led as Protector but built provincial congresses and a confederal republic with separated powers; parties did not exist yet, so this is inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The Instructions demand free ports and bar preference for one province's ports, opposing commercial privilege.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Instruction 3 promotes civil and religious liberty in the widest sense, which fits keeping politics free of denominational lines.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Anachronistic: an early 19th-century programme with no stance on technological civilization.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed; the programme's liberalism pulls one way and the Catholic legal order of the period the other.

national-resource-control.rationale: The programme defended provincial control of land and ports against Buenos Aires and the Portuguese; control by the community is inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The 1815 Reglamento redistributed land by need and by work, which implies that outcomes matter and not only how holdings arose; inferred from that program.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not a concern of the 1810s, and the programme's emphasis on free ports and provincial trade gives no clear lean on a financial tax; inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The Reglamento aimed to lift free Black and Indigenous people through land grants, suggesting adherents saw discrimination as a live obstacle; inferred and anachronistic.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Artigas's republican, Enlightenment-era programme rested on liberty and separated powers against arbitrary rule, so unjust law lacking binding force is inferred, not stated.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Industrial automation is anachronistic for a pastoral 1810s programme and no principle points either way.

multipolar-world.rationale: The Instructions favoured a confederation of sovereign provinces against Buenos Aires centralism and foreign rule, so power spread over several centres is inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The Reglamento granted land to those who work it, which loosely echoes labour as the source of value; inferred, not stated.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Artiguism joined patriotic independence with a land reform favouring the poor, so the two belonging together is inferred from that combination.

material-over-identity.rationale: The categories are anachronistic, and the programme pursued both material land reform and rights for Black and Indigenous people.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: There was no communist party in this period, and a federal republic of provincial militias and free ports does not fit party rule; inferred.

missingStatements.text: The capital of a federation should not be located in its largest and richest port city.
missingStatements.rationale: Instruction 19 requires the seat of the government of the United Provinces to be outside Buenos Aires, to avoid domination by one province.

missingStatements.text: Every region should be free to keep its own port customs and trade freely with the others without internal duties.
missingStatements.rationale: Instructions 12 to 14 declare free ports and bar duties on goods passing between provinces or preference for one province's ports.
missingStatements.declined: Internal-duties demand is historical and narrow; free-trade and tariffs statements cover the economics.

missingStatements.text: Land should be allotted first to the poorest, such as freed slaves, Indigenous people and landless country dwellers, provided they work it.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1815 Reglamento gave estancia plots to free Black people, zambos, Indigenous people and poor Creoles on condition of work, under the maxim that the most unfortunate be the most privileged.

notes: Debated whether the Reglamento was a social revolution or an order-and-production measure; La Nacion cites historian Rilla for the latter. Sources on slavery, the Church and criminal law were not found, so related answers are inferred or neutral.
